title: Coordinate and proper-support transport of supplied finite projective-line integrals
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\in\mathbb N$ with $NA=0$, and $t$ a normalized finite-root line transport [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Suppose supplied, for every scheme $T$ on which $N$ is invertible, a splitting $d_T$, the canonical base-change equations, and both supported diagonal integral identities exactly as in ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1Splitting, ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1BaseChange, and finiteP1DiagonalProperty [lem-sp-tower-p1-arbitrary-base-integrals]. Let $S$ be any such scheme. Put $P=\mathbf P(\operatorname{Option}(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(1)));S)$, $q:P\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $B=A_P(1)[2]$ and $L=A_S(1)[2]$ with the concrete finite-root line [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. On ordinary unbounded etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], there exist a trace-diagonal datum $k=(\tau:Rq_!B\to A_S,\delta:R\Delta_!A_P\to p_2^*B)$ [def-pur-td-datum] and an isomorphism $e:B\simeq q^*L$ such that both canonical coordinate integrals are identity, in precisely the convention SfDiagonalKernel.Integrals of [lem-sf-diagonal-kernel-integral-triangles]. Explicitly $\alpha_i$ is the canonical comparison for $p_i\Delta=1$, $\tau_1=\beta_1^{-1};q^*\tau$ followed by the unit comparison, and $\tau_2=Rp_{2!}(\operatorname{coordinate}(e)^{-1});\beta_2^{-1};q^*\tau$ followed by the unit comparison; then $\alpha_i;Rp_{i!}(\delta);\tau_i=1$ for $i=1,2$. Here $\beta_i$ is canonical proper exchange and coordinate(e) identifies the two pullbacks of B via e and qp1=qp2. The conclusion asserts only these coefficient maps and integral equations; no adjunction or triangle identity on general complexes is asserted.

source.place: The supported diagonal kernel, and the base-change identification of the two coordinate traces before applying the triangle calculations.

proof.text: Construct the graded polynomial renaming for ULift(Fin 2) equivalent to Option(ULift(Fin 1)). Its inverse induces the inverse Proj map. Base change the resulting integral-model isomorphism to obtain p1CoordinateIso over S; pullback.map proves that it commutes with the structure morphisms. These are explicit private constructions with complete proofs, as in SfP1CoordinateIntegrals; no affine-base hypothesis is used.

Unpack hi S hS to obtain its supported Ext representative kappa and the two ordinary integral equations. Apply sfP1IntegralTransport to the supplied t, d, hbc, the explicit coordinate isomorphism and kappa. This provides one trace-diagonal datum and conjugation equations comparing both compact-support integral composites with the corresponding ordinary composites. This transport statement applies to arbitrary bases and arbitrary supported Ext representatives.

Use the inverse of ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback along the standard-chart structure map as e. For each Boolean coordinate substitute the corresponding ordinary identity from hi into the transport equation. Functor.map_id and the inverse identities of the constant comparison reduce its conjugate to identity. The two resulting equations are definitionally SfDiagonalKernel.Integrals for the same datum and e.

proof_origin.place: Reuse the existing ordinary-to-compact-support transport theorem sfP1IntegralTransport, after the explicit graded coordinate renaming. Evaluate its two conjugated composites using the supplied integral equations; all combination steps are proved in Lean (S1, 2026-10-26).

lean.statement:
theorem finiteP1CoordinateKernel
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (N : ℕ) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    (d : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))),
      ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1Splitting A N hA t T hT)
    (hbc : ArbitraryBaseFiniteP1BaseChange A N hA t d)
    (hi : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))),
      finiteP1DiagonalProperty A N hA t d T hT)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) :
    ∃ k : TraceDiagonalDatum A
        (ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) ↘ S)
        (((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine
            ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) N A hA))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧),
      ∃ e : (((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine
            ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) N A hA))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≅
        (CoordinateTrace.pull A (ℙ(Option (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)); S) ↘ S)).obj
          (CoordinateTrace.shiftedLine A (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine S N A hA) 1),
        SfDiagonalKernel.Integrals A k
          (CoordinateTrace.shiftedLine A (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine S N A hA) 1) e
